Itineraries How to get around the city What is the weather like Gastronomic Guide Vegan Gastronomic Guide Events Blog Puerto Madero Instagram Facebook X-twitter Youtube LinkedIn The history of Puerto Madero is a living testimony of how a neglected area can be reborn in splendour. In the late 19th century, engineer Eduardo Madero's vision to build a port connecting Buenos Aires with Europe marked the beginning of a historic transformation. His proposal, approved in 1884 by President Julio Argentino Roca, led to the creation of a port that soon became a vital centre for the city's trade and port activity. Over time, Puerto Madero was transformed from a disused port area into a lively residential, gastronomic and commercial district. In 1989, an ambitious urban revitalisation plan was launched, which led to the creation of the Corporación Antiguo Puerto Madero. This initiative allowed for the restoration of the old docks, preserving their historic charm while adapting them to house modern lofts, offices and high-end restaurants. Today, Puerto Madero is one of Buenos Aires' most popular destinations, attracting tourists and locals alike with its unique blend of history and modernity. Its elegant pedestrian promenades, wide plazas and iconic buildings provide the perfect setting for strolling, enjoying local cuisine and admiring the beauty of the Rio de la Plata. Immerse yourself in the history and charm of Puerto Madero as you explore its cobblestone streets and old docks, which today are bustling with life and activity - a must-see for those who want to experience the best of Buenos Aires!
